colophon.title: How this site is built
colophon.lead: This portfolio is also a working product: a public site, a REST API and a private CMS. Here is how the parts fit together.
colophon.architecture: A Next.js site and a NestJS API, both on Vercel, with PostgreSQL on Neon and images in object storage. Visitors get pre-rendered pages; the API is only called to rebuild them.

contract.title: One contract
contract.text: Request and response schemas live in a shared Zod package. The API validates with it, the OpenAPI document is generated from it, and the dashboard forms use it.

publishing.title: Draft and published copies
publishing.text: Every item keeps an editable draft and a frozen published snapshot. Visitors only read snapshots, so edits are invisible until published.

revalidation.title: Static pages, refreshed on publish
revalidation.text: Publishing sends a signed request to the site, which rebuilds only the affected pages. No redeploy.

security.title: Security by default
security.text: Argon2id passwords, opaque server-side sessions in httpOnly cookies, rate limits shared across serverless instances, and uploads checked by their bytes, not their names.

architecture.title: Clean Architecture, kept small
architecture.text: Use cases depend on ports. Prisma, storage and email are adapters that can be swapped without touching business rules.

testing.title: Tested before deploy
testing.text: Unit, integration (against a real PostgreSQL) and end-to-end tests run in GitHub Actions before every deployment.
